players.product: NIPSCO GenCo generation and electric service built under IURC-approved special contracts and PPAs for Amazon and Alphabet data centers in Indiana

quarterly_data.signal: 10-K: in connection with the ADS Contract, NiSource expects to construct, through GenCo, 400 MW of new battery storage and a new power generation facility of two 1,300 MW CCGTs, expected to reach commercial operation between 2028 and 2032, plus related transmission and distribution assets, under EPC Contracts and equipment supply contracts already entered into; performing under any further data center contracts would require additional generation and transmission assets. In 2025 NiSource made $373.8 million of advanced deposits for project costs to secure certain long lead equipment related to data center generation assets.
quarterly_data.figure: 400 MW battery storage; two 1,300 MW CCGTs (commercial operation 2028-2032); $373.8 million advanced deposits for long-lead equipment (2025)

quarterly_data.signal: 10-K: 2025 capital expenditures totaled $4,051.6 million, of which NIPSCO Operations $2,508.9 million (including $1,171.2 million of Generation Transition Investments) and Columbia Operations $1,213.0 million; NIPSCO's owned generating facilities total 3,967 MW of capacity. Plant equipment purchase obligations (plant equipment, typically for generation assets, with long lead times that require payments made over time) totaled $103.3 million at December 31, 2025, of which $87.6 million falls in 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: 2025 capex $4,051.6 million; NIPSCO Operations $2,508.9 million; 3,967 MW owned generation; $103.3 million plant equipment purchase obligations

connects_to.relationship: NIPSCO GenCo generation and electric service for Amazon data centers in Indiana (special contract and PPA)

contracts.signal: 10-K: in September 2025 NIPSCO entered into the ADS Contract with Amazon Data Services, Inc. (ADS), a wholly-owned subsidiary of Amazon.com, Inc., to provide electricity to ADS' data centers under a capacity commitment beginning in 2027 and increasing annually to 2,400 MW by the end of 2032, and will construct up to 3,000 MW of dispatchable generation to provide that service. The initial term ends 15 years after the initial energization of ADS' initial data center; starting January 2027 ADS pays a fixed capacity charge and certain pass-through charges structured to return NiSource's invested capital over the fifteen-year initial term, with adjustment provisions designed to provide an unlevered internal rate of return within a defined range; Amazon.com, Inc. has guaranteed ADS' payment obligations. The contract was pending IURC approval at the time of filing.
contracts.units: capacity commitment rising to 2,400 MW by end of 2032; up to 3,000 MW of new dispatchable generation
